question: How much can one common unknown PPE correlation matrix change each of 20 cover-component and 30 temporal-contrast variances across the same qualified source-supported joint-age mixture?
conditioning: All 32,000 saved seed/native-row identities remain; 31,999 C_source rows define the conditional numerical target, with population denominator 31,999. The one empty-window row and the refused unconditional quantity are unchanged. No raw count table or age array is reopened.
finite_target: From each saved binary64 cover use the existing first-order PPE Jacobian. Form each older-minus-younger contrast gradient before multiplying by the four positive SDs and taking its outer product. Compensated binary64 outer sums divided by M_C produce symmetric finite Q. One common R is used over every age state: PPE variance is trace(Q R), R PSD with unit diagonal. Poaceae zero parameter SD removes only its free parameter axis, not its output uncertainty.
search_law: For each scalar and sign, retain exact identity and eight rank-one sign Gram candidates, then propose eight rank-two angle candidates with first angle zero and theta_j=2*pi*((k*m_j)%17)/17, k=1..8, m=(1,3,7). Use SLSQP analytic gradient, maxiter 200 and ftol 1e-13, no RNG and no outcome-driven restarts or changes. Normalization by trace(Q) is only for floating candidate search. Candidate feasibility and global certificates use unnormalized serialized Q as exact rationals; optimizer success does not certify global optimality, and no rank theorem is required.
certificate_law: Rational signed stereographic circle rows with 40-bit dyadic t make exact feasible Grams. For S=+Q or -Q, derive y_i=sum_j S_ij R_ij, try no padding then the frozen trace(Q)*2^e ladder, and certify Diag(y)-S PSD using all 15 exact principal minors. Keep the first passing padded candidate and the exact Gershgorin fallback y_i=S_ii+sum_j!=i abs(S_ij); choose the smaller certified upper bound. Convert the negative-sign bound into the original minimum. Preserve signed endpoints, attained witness values and gaps separately. Only an exact gap/trace(Q)<=1e-6 qualifies an endpoint as tight; otherwise retain a certified loose enclosure. Exact zero Q has zero endpoints and normalized gap zero with an identity witness. Nonzero nonpositive-trace or nonsymmetric Q is refused, never projected.
total_variance: Add Fraction.from_float(saved age variance) and Fraction.from_float(saved count variance) separately to each exact PPE endpoint. These fixed binary64 terms do not change with correlation. Different scalar extrema may use different R and do not define one jointly attaining covariance or simultaneous interval.
square_root_policy: Preserve signed exact total endpoints and exact order. If the outer lower endpoint is negative, return refused_signed_outer_bound and null SD displays; do not clip or intersect with a physical nonnegative domain. Exact zero is mathematically allowed. Otherwise show finite binary64 square roots explicitly as approximate, non-directed numerical displays. Positive underflow, overflow or an unsupported numeric domain refuses the display without changing the exact bounds.
precision_and_scope: Certificates are exact for supplied finite serialized Q, not the ideal unrounded age/PPE moment, the true physical integral or field uncertainty. Floating gradient/moment correspondence is checked separately at the declared tolerances, with no silent symmetrization or PSD clipping. Source-model assumptions, static geometry, parameter transfer, conditional pooled-count law and age/PPE independence are unchanged; a correlation sensitivity class supplies no adopted PPE distribution, ecological accuracy, posterior coverage or source/core/species admission.

Full numerical outputs remain local artifacts. No original count matrix, candidate table, saved-age matrix or publisher attachment is copied or redistributed.
